title: Kahana vs Kobo: The Book You Assign Together

metaDescription: Kobo is reading, catalogs, tracking, or ebook storefronts. Kahana is clubs and hubs around the books you actually read together.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Often described as the second-largest e-reader and ebook retailer in the world; launched 2009; localized in 16+ languages and available in 190+ countries.
Catalog of ≈5–6M titles spanning ebooks, audiobooks, newspapers, and magazines.
U.S. e-reader market share is niche (~3%); much stronger in Canada, French-speaking countries, the Netherlands, and other regions.

strengths.title: Strong international presence
strengths.detail: Localized stores and support in 190+ countries, with especially strong coverage in Europe and Canada.

strengths.title: Large multi-format catalog
strengths.detail: Millions of ebooks and audiobooks, plus newspapers and magazines, via e-readers and apps.

strengths.title: Cross-platform reading
strengths.detail: Award-winning e-readers and free apps for phones and tablets; reading syncs across devices.

strengths.title: Author-friendly self-publishing (Kobo Writing Life)
strengths.detail: Wide distribution for indie authors, revenue sharing, tools, and education via blogs and podcasts.

weaknesses.title: Limited U.S. presence
weaknesses.detail: Niche in the U.S. (~3% e-reader share) where Amazon dominates, weaker discoverability and network effects there.

weaknesses.title: Thinner ecosystem vs Amazon
weaknesses.detail: Fewer bundled services than Kindle + store + Prime; can reduce perceived value for some consumers.

weaknesses.title: DRM and regional availability
weaknesses.detail: Occasional complaints about DRM restrictions and titles varying by country.

weaknesses.title: UI / UX variability
weaknesses.detail: Generally well reviewed, but some users find store navigation and syncing less polished than Kindle.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Kobo is reading, catalogs, tracking, or ebook storefronts. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Open up to over 6 million eBooks and audiobooks on award-winning eReaders and the free Rakuten Kobo App.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Kobo side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Kobo you can use Ebook, Memberships, and Marketplaces as first-class product jobs. You need a dedicated reader, a giant store, or social tracking of everything you have ever read.

Using Kahana with Kobo

You can use both. Kobo keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep the reader or tracker you already use. Put the Club pick, discussion questions, and related files on Kahana so the book is a shared library item, not only a private progress bar.
